cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Choreographic devices are tools used to develop and structure movement material

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Repetition involves repeating a movement or phrase to create emphasis or recognition

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Unison means all dancers performing the same movement at the same time

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Canon is when dancers perform the same movement one after another in sequence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Accumulation builds a phrase by adding one movement at a time, retaining earlier movements

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Retrograde means performing a movement phrase in reverse order, like rewinding a video

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Fragmentation breaks a phrase into smaller parts which can be rearranged

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Development uses devices to transform original material so it remains connected but varied

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Choreographers choose devices to support their intention and communicate meaning

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Different devices create different effects — unison shows unity, canon shows ripple or wave

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: In AQA 8236, you must use choreographic devices in your NEA choreography and identify them in the written exam

cards.front: Recall a key point about Choreographic Devices
cards.back: Professional choreographers use devices to maintain audience interest and create variety

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — choreographic devices?
cards.back: 1. For Choreographic Devices questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Choreographic Devices 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
